prs.title: Add cache to `getSimplifiedConditionalType`
prs.author: ahejlsberg
prs.body: With this PR we consistently cache results in `getSimplifiedType`. Previously, we cached results for indexed access types but not conditional types. Found in performance experiments by Bun team.

prs.title: Replace nodeData interface with generated AST accessors
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
This ditches the dynamic dispatch with `nodeData` in favor of generated kind switches, like I did with `ForEachChild`.

| Metric | Merge base | Branch | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Binary file | 24,658,183 B | 23,810,311 B | **-847,872 B (-3.44%)** |
| Executable `.text` | 9,491,153 B | 9,366,833 B | **-124,320 B (-1.31%)** |
| Go PC/line metadata `.gopclntab` | 9,280,667 B | 8,583,938 B | **-696,729 B (-7.51%)** |
| Go type metadata `.go.type` | 3,447,248 B | 3,404,384 B | **-42,864 B (-1.24%)** |
| Symbols containing `tsc/internal/ast` | 6,331 | 2,682 | **-3,649 (-57.64%)** |
| AST pointer-receiver methods | 5,477 | 1,819 | **-3,658 (-66.79%)** |

It also makes compiling the ast package 5% faster. Some dispatch goes through small generated tables, because the fully switch-based code is slower.

Supersedes #64063. Part of the memory optimization stack summarized in #64734.

prs.title: Avoid allocating normalized types on interning cache hits
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
Union and intersection normalization builds temporary constituent lists even when an equivalent type already exists.

- Uses reentrant, bounded scratch space for canonicalization, while published types keep independently owned constituents.
- A fresh parse/bind/check of the compiler fixture used **8.51% fewer allocated bytes** and **18.26% fewer allocations**.
- Retained heap was effectively unchanged.

Part of the memory optimization stack summarized in #64734.

Replaces #64778, which GitHub closed as merged when the stack was reordered.

prs.title: Keep optional type-node and signature state out of hot records
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
Most type nodes never need outer type parameters, and most signatures have no type parameters, `this` parameter, predicate, or composite state.

- Moves optional outer type parameters out of type-node links (**32 → 16 bytes**).
- Moves optional signature state out of signatures (**128 → 80 bytes**).
- Historical VS Code retained-heap reductions were **0.43%** and **0.65%**, respectively.

Part of the memory optimization stack summarized in #64734.

Replaces #64785, which GitHub closed as merged when the stack was reordered.

prs.title: perf(checker): fast-path compareNodes for identical AST parent containers and use cmp.Compare
prs.author: hazyhaar
prs.body:
### Description

This PR introduces two focused optimizations in `tsc/internal/checker/utilities.go`:

1. **Fast-path in `compareNodes` for identical parent containers**:
   - When two AST nodes share the same syntactic parent container (`n1.Parent != nil && n1.Parent == n2.Parent`), they are guaranteed to reside in the exact same `SourceFile`.
   - In this common case, the comparison immediately returns `n1.Pos() - n2.Pos()`, entirely eliding the full AST ancestry traversal to root `SourceFile` nodes (`ast.GetSourceFileOfNode`) and the subsequent file index map lookups.
   - The ordering semantics are 100% identical to the existing implementation.

2. **64-bit integer overflow protection in `compareSymbolsWorker`**:
   - Replaces integer subtraction `int(ast.GetSymbolId(s1)) - int(ast.GetSymbolId(s2))` with `cmp.Compare(ast.GetSymbolId(s1), ast.GetSymbolId(s2))` for the unique `SymbolId` fallback comparison.
   - Operates directly on the native 64-bit `uint64` identifier without narrowing, eliminating any potential overflow risks.

### Validation & Test Results

- All targeted checker unit tests pass cleanly:
  `go test -race -count=1 ./tsc/internal/checker/...` -> **PASS**
- Full official Microsoft test suite (`TestLocal`) verified bit-exact with 0 regressions and 0 data races.
- Zero memory footprint impact (no allocations, pure in-place comparisons).

prs.title: [api] Fix named pipe / UDS creation
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body:
One semi-related fix per commit.

- af47f842b1e134d244f477c73e69b7f0b946a1a4: when creating a UDS for an API client, create a tmp directory first and set permissions on the socket path to 0o600
- 058a1edff004fae4d5e8b124a51af3c5890e6a8b: when an LSP client asks for an API socket to be created by a specific name, interpret that as the name of the tmp directory to be created and make the socket path `${tmpdir}/socket`, so the same strategy as above can be used
- 416b01337e976b2346cb45c30fc1d9628d6731dd: use a random pipe name on Windows when spawning the sync API

prs.title: Avoid weakset for executed generators
prs.author: dragomirtitian
prs.body:
Fixes #64829

This PR uses a symbol to keep track of executed generators.

There is a small change in behavior, since now the maker is global. However I don't think this is significant. The whole point of the check is to ensure generators are not reused since unlike promises which you can `await` multiple times, you can't `yield* ` a generator multiple times. So using a global marker is probably better preventing reuse even across batches.

prs.title: Fix release pipeline tests and workflow
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
- The version swap breaks a help test; fix it
- The token perms requested were not enough, and had odd errors on pipeline failure.

prs.title: Ban network paths wholesale
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
Simply trying to touch a network path may automatically send credentials over the network to a server. Just ban them entirely, across the board.

There are nice errors where possible, otherwise the funcs that hit the OS just reject them entirely.

Checking is cheap; max looking at the first 4 bytes of a path.

prs.body: Instead of using tmp, which is world-writable on Linux etc.

prs.title: Escape quotes in synthesized module specifiers
prs.author: RyanCavanaugh
prs.body:
Fixes cases where package.json could have a module specifier that closed the import name, making the importing file syntactically invalid or unexpected:
```ts
import * as foo from "uneescaped"string";
```

I am not attached to this generated testcase, it's not great, but does do the job. Open to changing it to a matrix of single cases if anyone cares.
